title: A cast seeds decisions from builder_check
intention: A ticket's first rehearsal starts from the builder's answers the cast already wrote, because the cast seeds the ticket's decisions from its /sorted builder_check instead of leaving the reader to rediscover them as gaps.
why: Peer F35 (2026-10-08), first framed after 80518446bfc8: a cast already answers the builder's questions at /sorted (builder_check), but the answers ride the ticket only as builder_notes, which the rehearsal reader does not tie to any step, so the first rehearsal pass rediscovers them as gaps. Measured: 80518446bfc8 pass 1 read 40 gaps of one cause; 8y ran 12 passes. Until this lands the builder writes D-lines by hand before the first rehearsal (done on 42075a49c121) — policy where the cast door can carry it (Law 1, Law 4).
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel: the builder_check answers are settled at /sorted and the rehearsal reader re-derives them as gaps — 80518446bfc8's first pass read 40 gaps of one cause) and CP4 (rehearsal is paid per pass; Akien ruled it temporary scaffolding, so its cost is kept small).
how: cairn/tools/base/transitions.py cast_ticket(): after every lack check passes and before the write, when the doc carries no decisions (absent or an empty list) and its sorted_berth's answers.builder_check is a non-blank string, the doc gains decisions = [{n: 1, text: 'D1 (the /sorted builder_check): <builder_check verbatim>', by: actor, step: 'cast', source: 'sorted', at: <utc iso>}]. A doc that already carries decisions is untouched. One new proof in cairn/tools/base/proofs/.
